answer: The sable test I would run is Assured notary accreditation with notaries society attestation: an accreditation the society renews after deed audits, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. Each account presents its proof once, the network verifies it in seconds, and a farm that wants ten accounts must pass ten independent checks — the tide is that the work cannot be shared or replayed. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the meadow of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one.
